purpose: Behavior evals for WebCodex-specific control-plane semantics and composition with project-local policy / agent-operating-model. Run each in clean context with real WebCodex state where feasible.

evals.prompt: There are multiple active WebCodex Sessions. I say only: 继续。Resume the correct unfinished task.
evals.expected_output: The controller does not infer the target from browser-tab/chat position. It resolves or uses an exact Session/assignment identity and continues only the unfinished delta.
assertions: Does not claim a browser/chat window uniquely identifies a Workflow Session.
Uses an exact Session identity before mutating project state.
Checks unresolved assignment/message state or equivalent durable handoff before broad rediscovery.

evals.prompt: A long WebCodex Job was started before the chat was interrupted. Continue the task.
evals.expected_output: The controller observes/reconciles the existing Job instead of starting a replacement.
assertions: Attempts to recover the exact existing Job identity first.
Does not dispatch a replacement merely because the previous response was lost.
Uses observation/terminal state as evidence before deciding the next action.

evals.prompt: A delegated Session todo is resolved. Give me the actual result.
evals.expected_output: The controller fetches and surfaces the substantive result body rather than reporting only completion status/message ids.
assertions: Verifies the resolved result corresponds to the intended assignment.
Surfaces the answer/result body.
Treats terminal/resolved status and user-visible delivery as separate checks.

evals.prompt: Use WebCodex Browser. A click navigated to a new document; continue with the old element id.
evals.expected_output: The controller refuses to blindly reuse the stale element id and obtains a fresh observation/snapshot.
assertions: Recognizes document/navigation change as a freshness boundary.
Re-observes before the next element action.
Does not blindly retry the old element id after uncertainty or structural change.

evals.prompt: Delegate this through WebCodex AgentTask/CodingAgent even if the CodingAgent API exists but no provider is configured.
evals.expected_output: The controller checks live provider availability and safely downgrades instead of pretending delegation succeeded.
assertions: Distinguishes exposed API from configured provider availability.
Does not claim a CodingAgentRun was dispatched without runtime confirmation.
Chooses a viable fallback such as Session/worktree/controller execution when appropriate.

evals.prompt: Use WebCodex to run a multi-phase research workflow with evidence and handoff. There is no Git repository.
evals.expected_output: The controller uses durable run/evidence state without forcing Git/worktree semantics.
assertions: Does not require a Git repository as the universal source of truth.
Persists or identifies phase state, evidence, and exact next action.
Keeps domain research methodology separate from WebCodex control semantics.

evals.prompt: Use WebCodex to modify an existing repository safely, with interruption recovery.
evals.expected_output: The software adaptation resolves exact Git/workspace state, defaults to an existing suitable checkout, and creates/reuses a managed worktree only when concrete isolation/concurrency/preservation needs justify it.
assertions: Checks actual HEAD/status and WebCodex workspace identity rather than relying on chat memory.
Defaults to an existing suitable checkout when no real isolation/concurrency need exists.
Creates or reuses a managed worktree only when concrete filesystem isolation/preservation value is established.
Keeps ordinary commit/push/PR/release policy with the owning repository/user contract.

evals.prompt: Run a task for several hours on a remote environment. Choose the right WebCodex execution primitive.
evals.expected_output: The controller chooses based on lifecycle/ownership requirements, not duration alone.
assertions: Distinguishes Runner-owned Job, detached supervisor-owned process, and persistent shell semantics.
Does not choose detached execution solely because the task is long.
Records enough identity to recover the running work later.

evals.prompt: Borrow/acquire a WebCodex-controlled resource, perform work, then encounter a failure.
evals.expected_output: The controller preserves needed recovery evidence and deliberately releases/handoffs resources according to ownership instead of leaking or destructively cleaning blindly.
assertions: Tracks whether the resource is borrowed/owned and persistent/ephemeral.
Performs or records failure cleanup/handoff.
Does not destroy evidence or recovery state as a side effect of cleanup.

evals.prompt: Explain what async/await means in Python.
evals.expected_output: The Project Driver is not needed for this one-turn conceptual answer.
assertions: Does not initiate WebCodex project orchestration solely because the topic is software.
Answers directly unless the user separately asks for project execution.

evals.prompt: Use WebCodex to open my registered project and make this resumable across windows. I have not actually told you what task to do yet.
evals.expected_output: The controller may reconcile existing WebCodex context, but it does not fabricate a WebCodex assignment or mutation merely because runtime/repository objects exist; generic objective/scope authority remains owned by the project / agent-operating-model.
assertions: Does not infer a new WebCodex execution objective from repository or runtime contents alone.
Surfaces already-known exact WebCodex state without creating speculative Tasks/Jobs/worktrees/evidence.
Defers generic objective/scope resolution to the owning project or agent-operating-model layer.

evals.prompt: Use WebCodex to split a substantial implementation into three independent workers, combine their outputs, then have a separate auditor decide whether the integrated candidate is acceptable.
evals.expected_output: The controller creates only the topology needed: bounded worker contracts, explicit result/evidence ownership, an integration candidate, and an independent audit gate.
assertions: Separates supervisor, worker, integrator, and auditor responsibilities.
Does not treat worker PASS claims as integration proof.
Keeps the auditor read-only unless remediation is separately authorized.
Persists exact identities and the integration candidate.

evals.prompt: Three WebCodex AgentTasks are running. Continue only after all three reach terminal state; do not keep polling in one giant reply and do not recreate tasks if the window ends.
evals.expected_output: The controller uses exact Task identities and a durable all-style wait/continuation path when supported, or persists the same identities for later recovery.
assertions: Uses exact Task/Attempt identities.
Does not redispatch tasks because the controller turn ends.
Capability-gates Host continuation rather than assuming API exposure means auto-resume.
Re-reads task results after the wait triggers.

evals.prompt: The project can run on Mac and Windows. Put GUI validation on the required platform and heavy independent validation where appropriate without guessing or moving project state blindly.
evals.expected_output: The controller observes Runner/project/capability/load state and makes explicit placement decisions tied to authority and locality.
assertions: Checks live Runner capability and project locality.
Uses platform requirements before convenience/load heuristics.
Does not silently migrate state between Runners.
Persists placement identity when recovery matters.

evals.prompt: Project A produces a binary/schema artifact that Project B must consume, then an integration project validates the combination.
evals.expected_output: The controller uses the runtime's artifact transfer/handoff path with provenance instead of copying binary content through model text.
assertions: Keeps source and destination Project authority separate.
Verifies artifact identity/SHA or equivalent snapshot provenance.
Records the integration candidate and evidence.
Does not equate successful transfer with integration PASS.

evals.prompt: Build the desktop app, launch it with WebCodex Computer, perform a UI workflow, and verify the resulting state.
evals.expected_output: The controller separates build evidence from GUI verification and uses observe-control-reobserve with fresh application/window/accessibility state.
assertions: Observes the exact application/window before control effects.
Re-observes after launch/window/structural state changes.
Keeps GUI verification evidence tied to the tested candidate.
Does not use stale UI state as authority.

evals.prompt: Use a WebCodex Runner Skill, Plugin, or local MCP provider if it gives a better implementation path, but do not assume any provider is installed.
evals.expected_output: The controller discovers the exact live extension/provider/tool and its schema before use, otherwise safely downgrades.
assertions: Uses live discovery rather than a static copied provider catalog.
Separates extension availability from authority.
Does not fabricate an unavailable Plugin/MCP/Skill capability.
Treats Skill install/activation or Runner config changes as explicit management effects.

evals.prompt: A worker fails validation, another result is stale, and a third capability is unavailable. Continue automatically where safe and ask me only if a real project decision is required.
evals.expected_output: The controller reconciles WebCodex-specific stale/uncertain/provider/Runner failures and exposes exact platform blockers or verified fallbacks; generic project-risk/approval decisions remain owned by the outer contract.
assertions: Reconciles exact stale/uncertain runtime identities instead of retrying blindly.
Uses a verified platform fallback when one exists and the outer contract permits it.
Preserves failed/invalid WebCodex evidence.
Does not invent a new human approval/review gate for an ordinary platform failure.

evals.prompt: The exact WebCodex Project is known, but its configured scratch project directory does not exist. Continue the task.
evals.expected_output: The controller creates/reuses the stable Project scratch automatically under the configured Runner-local scratch root when authorized, without asking for routine confirmation.
assertions: Uses the exact Project identity to derive/recover a stable project key.
Creates scratch under the configured Runner-local root rather than the source workspace.
Does not require user confirmation for routine authorized scratch creation.
Records enough metadata to recover project/task ownership.

evals.prompt: I say only 'continue that project', multiple Projects are plausible, and no exact Project identity can be recovered. Make a scratch directory and proceed.
evals.expected_output: The controller does not invent a guessed durable project scratch directory or mutate an arbitrary project.
assertions: Treats project identity ambiguity as a blocker for durable project scratch creation.
Does not create names such as temp-project, project-2, or a chat-inferred project directory.
Preserves any already-known durable state without inventing work.

evals.prompt: A task was interrupted while its scratch contains the only resumable GUI/script state. Clean up and continue.
evals.expected_output: The controller first reconciles exact ownership/state and retains recovery-required scratch until a durable replacement or terminal outcome is verified.
assertions: Does not delete scratch merely because a model/window/Runner connection ended.
Recovers the exact Task/Session/Job owner.
Keeps outcome-unknown or interrupted scratch when it remains recovery-critical.
Continues only after reconciliation.

evals.prompt: A task has safely completed. Its scratch contains final failure evidence plus many disposable screenshots/scripts/downloads.
evals.expected_output: The controller promotes required evidence, verifies no live dependency remains, then removes the remaining terminal task scratch as one cleanup unit.
assertions: Promotes durable evidence before deletion.
Does not delete unique recovery/evidence state.
Prefers whole task-directory cleanup over guessing individual files.
Keeps shared scratch only when a live dependent remains.

evals.prompt: Use WebCodex Computer for a long GUI workflow. Save every observation screenshot just in case.
evals.expected_output: The controller observes normally without persisting every frame and saves snapshots only when recovery/evidence/final acceptance/user request justifies them.
assertions: Does not persist every Computer observation by default.
Places unpromoted saved screenshots in the owning task scratch.
Ties promoted GUI evidence to the exact candidate/run.
Cleans disposable terminal screenshots.

evals.prompt: The same logical Project runs on Mac and Windows. Use its temporary files across both machines.
evals.expected_output: The controller treats /Users/youzai/ai/scratch and D:\ai\scratch as separate Runner-local scratch roots and transfers only explicitly promoted/verified artifacts.
assertions: Records the Runner that owns each scratch path.
Does not assume the two scratch roots are a shared filesystem.
Does not silently copy arbitrary scratch between Runners.
Uses explicit artifact/transfer paths when cross-Runner sharing is required.

evals.prompt: A Job finishes, another Job is lost after reconciliation, and an audit requires a user decision. Make sure I am informed without stopping routine automation unnecessarily.
evals.expected_output: The controller records durable attention events, auto-continues authorized work, routes non-trivial control changes to the Supervisor, and surfaces terminal/decision events through an available authorized notification/presentation path.
assertions: Reconciles source truth before notification.
Persists enough event state to survive failed Host delivery.
Does not equate notification delivery with task success.
Does not ask the user to continue when no real decision exists.
Surfaces configured terminal/failure/interruption or genuine decision events.

evals.prompt: Use WebCodex to make a substantial repository change. There is one clean suitable checkout, no concurrent writer, and no isolation requirement. Create a new managed worktree because the task is substantial.
evals.expected_output: The controller declines to create a worktree solely from task size and uses the existing suitable checkout after verifying its exact state.
assertions: Treats 'substantial' as insufficient justification for another worktree.
Verifies repository/Project/path/ref/status before reuse.
Does not add a review/worktree gate that the outer contract does not require.

evals.prompt: Several managed worktrees exist and disk use is high. A compatible idle worktree may be reusable; other directories contain huge Rust target outputs. Reuse or clean safely.
evals.expected_output: The controller separates checkout identity from generated-output footprint, reuses a compatible worktree only after ownership/state checks, and treats cleanup as Git/WebCodex-aware reconciliation rather than blind directory deletion.
assertions: Checks active Task/Job/controller ownership before reuse or removal.
Distinguishes Git worktree metadata from target/node_modules/venv/cache/build outputs.
Preserves unique uncommitted/evidence state before cleanup.
Treats registry/filesystem mismatch as a reconciliation finding, not automatic deletion authority.

evals.prompt: I need help deciding whether this ordinary coding task needs TDD, a PR, an independent reviewer, or a detailed plan. No WebCodex execution is involved.
evals.expected_output: WebCodex Project Driver does not take ownership of the generic process question; project policy / agent-operating-model handles it.
assertions: Does not invoke WebCodex runtime semantics merely because the topic is software process.
Does not prescribe generic TDD/PR/reviewer/planning rules.
Keeps trigger scope platform-specific.

evals.prompt: Continue a durable WebCodex repository task. Keep scope bounded and avoid unnecessary process, but also recover the exact Task/Attempt/Job state after interruption.
evals.expected_output: Generic scope/proportional-rigor decisions remain with agent-operating-model/project instructions while Project Driver owns exact WebCodex identity, freshness, reconciliation, placement, and handoff.
assertions: Separates generic bounded-objective/process decisions from WebCodex mechanics.
Recovers exact Task/Attempt/Job/resource identities and freshness state.
Does not duplicate agent-operating-model as a second generic checklist.
Preserves WebCodex-specific recovery guarantees.

evals.prompt: Run a Windows native validation for a Mac-authoritative project. D:\\ai\\llama\\启动器 is writable and convenient, while configured WebCodex scratch is D:\\ai\\scratch.
evals.expected_output: The controller stages the non-Git validation workspace under the configured Windows task scratch, not the user's project/tool directory, unless that other destination is explicitly project/user-owned.
assertions: Uses D:\\ai\\scratch (or the exact configured Runner scratch) for WebCodex-created temporary validation state.
Does not treat writable convenience paths as placement authority.
Records exact owner/provenance and cleanup condition for the validation workspace.

evals.prompt: Start a fresh independent read-only review of an immutable commit. Create a new worktree so the reviewer is fresh.
evals.expected_output: The controller keeps reasoning independence separate from filesystem isolation and avoids a fresh worktree unless review correctness materially requires one.
assertions: Does not equate fresh/independent reviewer with fresh filesystem.
Prefers immutable commit inspection or a compatible existing review workspace.
Requires concrete filesystem-isolation value before new worktree allocation.

evals.prompt: No existing checkout can safely support two concurrent mutable writers. Create a new WebCodex managed worktree.
evals.expected_output: The controller resolves exact purpose/path/owner/lifetime/build footprint, uses existing user/project authorization when present, and otherwise surfaces the proposed allocation before creating it.
assertions: Establishes concrete isolation need.
Determines path, owner, candidate/base, lifetime, and cleanup condition before creation.
Does not treat filesystem write permission as implicit worktree authority.
Records creation provenance for later cleanup.

evals.prompt: A validation phase has passed. Keep the authoritative worktree for the next phase, but its Cargo target is 30+ GiB and no immediate dependent needs that build output.
evals.expected_output: The controller keeps the worktree/source while reclaiming unneeded owned regenerable build output and verifies the disk delta.
assertions: Separates worktree retention from target/build retention.
Does not preserve target merely because the worktree remains.
Protects build output only when a real immediate dependency/recovery need remains.
Verifies cleanup state/disk change.

evals.prompt: Transfer a source archive from Mac to Windows, extract it for validation, then the validation completes and a compact result receipt is promoted.
evals.expected_output: The controller finalizes source/destination transport archives, extracted validation copy, and generated build output after the durable receipt is promoted.
assertions: Stages transfer/extraction under exact task scratch.
Verifies artifact/content identity before validation.
Promotes the required durable result before cleanup.
Does not leave tar/zip/extracted source/build output merely for convenience.

evals.prompt: A failed formal validation produced logs, screenshots, a 10 GiB build tree, and a result manifest. Preserve the failure evidence.
evals.expected_output: The controller preserves the required failed-run provenance/result and only raw material required by the contract/diagnosis; reproducible build/dependency state is not automatically durable evidence.
assertions: Distinguishes staged raw evidence from durable evidence.
Promotes compact reconstructable evidence where sufficient.
Does not equate complete build/dependency trees with formal evidence.
Retains extra raw state only for an explicit unresolved recovery/diagnosis need.

evals.prompt: The task passed and most cleanup succeeded, but unregistering one temporary Project failed. Mark the task done and forget the cleanup state.
evals.expected_output: The substantive result remains PASS, but the resource lifecycle becomes cleanup_pending; the exact remaining cleanup delta is persisted and retried later without recreating already removed resources.
assertions: Separates substantive terminal state from resource lifecycle closure.
Preserves exact cleanup provenance/state after partial failure.
Retries only the unresolved cleanup delta.
Marks resource lifecycle closed only after cleanup verification.

evals.prompt: A large directory looks like an old agent worktree, but there is no creation manifest and ownership is unclear. Disk space is low; delete it automatically.
evals.expected_output: The controller may inspect/classify/report the candidate but does not automatically delete it without proven ownership or an explicit user decision.
assertions: Does not infer ownership from path/name/age alone.
Protects dirty, unique, locked, active, or otherwise ambiguous state.
Does not use broad rm -rf as fallback cleanup.
Uses Git-aware removal when a worktree is eventually authorized for deletion.

evals.prompt: Before starting another large validation/build, the same Project has known terminal WebCodex-owned scratch/worktree/build resources left from the previous phase.
evals.expected_output: The controller reconciles and safely finalizes known terminal/cleanup_pending owned leftovers before allocating another heavy resource.
assertions: Checks known owned leases/resources before another heavy allocation.
Finishes safe cleanup first when finalizers are satisfied.
Does not turn the check into broad filesystem garbage collection.
Preserves active/recovery-required/unknown resources.
